title: NHRP: added fields for ipv6 addresses, given code 0x2001
description:
I added address field for ipv6 addresses to nhrp and new checks for address' length in packet-nhrp.c. The protocol is now registered in ethertype table under the code 0x2001 like in GRE table. In order to avoid conflicts CGMP has code 0x2000 now in ethertype table also like in GRE. Ethertype has NHRP as subdissector now.

I think that NHRP may be soon used in Ethertype so I added its dissector to Ethertype table. I have given to dissector the code 0x2001 like it is in GRE to not create confusions. This is the reason I also changed CGMP code to 0x2000 in Ethertype. Must be strange when almost equal packet that only differ in "GRE over IP"/"GRE over IPv6" are dissected as two different protocols

> CGMP has code 0x2000 now in ethertype table also like in GRE.

GRE has Cisco CDP as 0x2000, not CGMP. Those are different protocols.

GRE has a 2 octet "Protocol Type" field which is defined in RFC 2784 to be Ethertypes, but in practice there are several values which are not registered Ethertypes but used in GRE anyway.

Cisco has various PIDs that are used together with SNAP headers and the Cisco OUI that are also two bytes and are not Ethertypes (but look like them). Sometimes similar values are chosen.

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/dissectors/packet-gre.h

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/cisco_pid.h
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/dissectors/packet-cisco-oui.c

I'm not sure that any of these unregistered values should be registered in the Ethertype table, as opposed to in the GRE (and Cisco OUI for LLC/SNAP) tables.

> Must be strange when almost equal packet that only differ in "GRE over IP"/"GRE over IPv6" are dissected as two different protocols

Can you provide sample captures demonstrating this? Presumably "GRE over IP" and "GRE over IPv6" should both use the same GRE-related dissector table for dissecting the various values which are not actually registered Ethertypes?

Yes, I really shouldn't change codes and add nhrp to Ethertype but in packet-sll.c code says: if the type is GRE over IP then dissection goes with GRE table and if the type if GRE over IPv6 ethertype table is used to find the dissector. This only happens when there's GRE incapsulation. There may be other protocols that are mistakenly dissected using ethertype table. I locally changed packet-sll to not use ethertype table for nhrp in GRE-incapsulated packets but it doesn't seem to be an optimal solution in future. I don't know if nhrp is the only protocol with this problem. If not — maybe an additional table is needed

The answer may be to have the same handling for `ARPHRD_IP6GRE` as currently done for `ARPHRD_IPGRE`. That would be simpler  It would be easier with a sample capture, however, if you can provide one.

The entry in https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes/LINKTYPE_LINUX_SLL.html mentions that "If the ARPHRD_ type is ARPHRD_IPGRE (778), the protocol type field contains a GRE protocol type," but doesn't say anything about `ARPHRD_IP6GRE`. Same for https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes/LINKTYPE_LINUX_SLL2.html
Providing a sample capture would also have made it clearer that your issue concerned captures with the Linux "cooked capture" / any device / SLL link-layer type.

[nhrp_ipv6.pcap](/uploads/61721a9ebb27c848d027d59ed67d9b27/nhrp_ipv6.pcap)
Pcaps with NHRP incapsulated in GRE. Now it is dissected with Ethertype table as CGMP

commits_data.title: NHRP: added fields for ipv6 addresses
commits_data.message:
NHRP: added fields for ipv6 addresses

Added fields for IPv6 addresses to packet-nhrp.c that clone fields for IPv4
addresses. Dissection is done with check for length 16. Additionaly changed
dissection for Extension data: if length of extension is less than source
length + 4 the source length is not added to tree — the whole remainder is
considered as data.
